doctrine_checks.details: Spec declares required geometry inputs (SF, LF) and does not compute them. PaintScope is referenced as source.
All tasks declare UOM. Edge tasks use LF, field tasks use SF, discrete tasks use EA. Production rates match task UOMs.
Edge tasks explicitly require LF from PaintScope (ceiling_line_lf, trim_line_lf). Spec does not assume or invent LF values.
Spec correctly positions itself to receive geometry from PaintScope and pass to Estimation Engine.
Coverage rates are per-gallon, consumable rates are per-SF/LF/EA. No total quantities assumed.

issues.description: All production rates are placeholders and require field calibration before use.
issues.suggested_fix: Conduct time studies on residential repaint jobs to establish baseline rates.

issues.description: Condition-based consumable multipliers (good vs fair) need validation against actual job data.
issues.suggested_fix: Track spackle, caulk, and sandpaper usage on real jobs by condition category.

issues.description: Spot prime tasks are count-based (EA) but repair counts vary widely by condition. May need SF-based alternative for large repair areas.
issues.suggested_fix: Consider adding area-based spot prime task for fair condition with extensive repairs.

issues.description: Freehand cut-in rates are highly skill-dependent. Current rates assume journeyman-level skill.
issues.suggested_fix: Add skill-level factor modifier or provide rate ranges for apprentice/journeyman/master.

issues.description: Spec assumes latex-over-latex. Alkyd-over-existing scenarios may need different prep.
issues.suggested_fix: Document alkyd compatibility in research notes; add compatibility rule if needed.

summary: Residential repaint wall spec is doctrine-compliant: SF field + LF edges with proper PaintScope geometry sourcing. Prep modules correctly differentiated by surface condition. All rates require calibration before production use.
review_notes: Spec correctly separates good vs fair condition prep as modular alternatives.
Edge strategies (freehand vs tape-line) are properly modeled as separate modules.
LF tasks explicitly require PaintScope inputs - no internal LF computation.
Protection setup/teardown appropriately models residential occupied environment.
Quality effects adjust sanding intensity and edge discipline appropriately.
